workflow: A text-building operation receives an empty input whose data pointer is null.
The operation computes a transfer length of zero but continues through the normal append path.
It invokes a low-level memory-copy routine with the null pointer despite the zero length.
The pointer precondition is violated, producing undefined-behavior diagnostics instead of returning successfully for the empty input.
summary: Zero-length text append passes null storage to memory copy
decision_reason: The failure mechanism is materially the same: an empty buffer yields a possibly null data pointer, and a zero-length low-level memory transfer is still invoked without guarding the null pointer.
